name: Shan
notes:
Shan (တႆး, Tai Long), a Southwestern Tai (Tai-Kadai) language of Shan State, Myanmar, ~3-4 million speakers, the majority/regional language of Shan State. Script: the modern reformed Shan alphabet (Unicode Myanmar block, 1950s systematic-tone-marking reform) — a Burmese-derived ABUGIDA whose 19 base consonant letters carry an inherent /a/ (declared via `inherent_vowel`), modified by dependent vowel signs and, distinctively, by dedicated TONE-MARK letters at the end of the syllable. GRAPHEME KEYS: consonants and vowel signs follow the standard letter chart ('Shan alphabet', Wikipedia; consonant IPA cross-checked against PHOIBLE's shan1277 inventory) -- note `သ`, Burmese θ historically, is repurposed in Shan for /s/, not /θ/ (Shan has no /θ/ in its PHOIBLE inventory), and `ရ`, historically /r/, is kept polysemous /j~l/ reflecting the well-documented Tai r>y/l merger rather than invented as a third, unattested consonant. TONE MARKS earn grapheme keys under design-constraint test 2: each mark spells a single suprasegmental unit (one lexical tone), not a concatenable segment, exactly the way this dataset already treats stress marks and vowel length; the five tone-mark keys here (rising is the UNMARKED default, so five marks cover the remaining five of six tones Wikipedia's Shan-language article describes for unchecked syllables) are mapped to the IPA pitch contours the source gives (rising ˨˦ unmarked / low ˩ / mid-falling ˧˨ / high ˥ / high-falling-creaky ˦˨ˀ / emphatic ˧˦˧). KNOWN GAP, documented rather than resolved by guessing: checked (stopped) syllables contrast only FOUR tones by the cited source, and the mark-to-tone correspondence in that environment is not yet split out with a `positional_graphemes`/coda-conditioned rule -- left for a follow-up cited pass. STRESS: Shan is a tone language without a separate stress system in the cited sources; no `stress` block, a documented exemption (tone marks carry the prosodic information instead). SMOKE CHECKS against `shn_mymr_broad.tsv` (WikiPron, broad transcription): ငဝ်း -> gold 'ŋ a w ˥' (ξ=ŋ, inherent a, ဝ=w, း=˥ high tone, matches); ငိင်း -> gold 'ŋ i ŋ ˥' (င=ŋ, ိ=i, coda ‌င=ŋ, း=˥, matches); ငူဝ်း -> gold 'ŋ oː ˥' (င=ŋ, ူ=oː, ဝ်=silent killed-w coda per the source's 'killed consonant' convention, း=˥, matches). TIER: `research` -- sourced (PHOIBLE; Wikipedia Shan alphabet/language; r12a script notes), tone-as-prosody exemption documented, and `shn_mymr_broad.tsv` (2607 rows, WikiPron/Wiktionary scrape, `crowd-scraped` provenance, registered below) is scored in `scripts/benchmark.py` with a PER recorded in `benchmarks/results.json`.

TONE PLACEMENT AUDIT (this pass). Thai and Lao, the closely related Tai systems already worked out in this dataset, both COMPUTE tone from consonant class and rime shape, and both had a tone-PLACEMENT gap as their remaining defect. Shan differs: it writes tone with dedicated, unambiguous tone-mark letters (already declared above), so that prior does not transfer as a rule -- it had to be measured, not assumed. `scripts/fold_shn_notation.py` scores the row as-is, then folds tone identity out entirely on both sides, then folds tone PLACEMENT only (move the mark to a fixed position, keep identity and order, mirroring the Thai/Lao instrument), then folds vowel length as well. Tone-placement folding barely moves the number (0.3040 against an as-scored 0.3057): the Thai/Lao gap does not transfer, exactly as the explicit-tone-letter analysis predicts. Folding tone identity out entirely gives 0.2547, just above the 0.25 production threshold; folding vowel length as well gives 0.2777. `valid_ceiling.wikipron` records the tone-identity number as the honest ceiling, with the placement negative result in its citation.

COMPOUND VOWELS ⟨ိူ ို⟩ (fixed this pass). The vowel signs ⟨ိ⟩ (i-sign) and ⟨ူ/ု⟩ (u/o-signs) combine to spell two vowels neither sign spells alone: ⟨ိူ⟩ /ɤ/ and ⟨ို⟩ /ɯ/ before a written coda consonant, lengthening to /ɤː/ /ɯː/ in the open-syllable spelling that marks the vowel with a killed ⟨ဝ်⟩ coda the same way `ူဝ်` already does for /oː/ (r12a Shan Script Notes; both /ɤ/ and /ɯ/ are in PHOIBLE's shan1277 inventory already carried in `phonemes`). Before this pass neither combination had a grapheme key, so the tokenizer read the two signs as sequential /i/ + /u~oː/ and, where a killed ⟨ဝ်⟩ followed, added a spurious /w/: ⟨မိူင်း⟩ 'country' read /miuŋ˥/-shaped strings for gold /mɤŋ˥/, ⟨ႁိူဝ်း⟩ 'boat' read /hioːw˥/ for gold /hɤː˥/. Measured against `shn_mymr_broad.tsv`: 179 rows spell bare ⟨ိူ⟩, 135 spell bare ⟨ို⟩, 71 spell ⟨ိူဝ်⟩ and 30 spell ⟨ိုဝ်⟩ -- 415 of 2607 rows (15.9%), checked row-by-row and consistently read /ɤ(ː)/ or /ɯ(ː)/ in the gold with no counterexample found. The four sequences are declared as their own multi-codepoint graphemes (the same flat-table mechanism Thai's ⟨ีย ือ ัว⟩ circumfixes use), which the tokenizer's maximal-munch matching picks over the shorter single-sign entries wherever they occur; no positional or coda-conditioned rule was needed. This moved `shn_mymr_broad.tsv` PER from 0.3419 (pre-fix, this session's measurement; 0.3348 is the previously committed board figure, n=2604 against this session's n=2607) to 0.3057.

LOAN-SOUND LETTER ⟨ႀ⟩ (fixed this pass). ⟨ႀ⟩, absent from the earlier grapheme table, is a dedicated letter for /θ/ used in loanwords (r12a Shan Script Notes: 'for non-Shan sounds'); PHOIBLE's shan1277 inventory does not carry native /θ/, so this is added as the loan-sound letter it is, not folded into the native-consonant ⟨သ⟩=/s/ analysis above. All 8 `shn_mymr_broad.tsv` rows containing ⟨ႀ⟩ read /θ/ in the gold; the letter is declared with no counterexample.

REFUSED. The gold rows scored above at the 0.2547 tone-identity ceiling still leave a residual this pass did not investigate: several multi-syllable and compound entries (e.g. ⟨လွင်ႈၵူႈ⟩, ⟨ၸဝ်ႈၼႃႈတီႈ⟩) mismatch on segment count or word-boundary grouping rather than on any single grapheme, which looks like a tokenization/compounding question distinct from both the tone and vowel-digraph findings above and is left for a follow-up cited pass rather than guessed at here. The four-tone/six-tone checked-syllable gap noted above is likewise still open.

wikipron.citation: shn_mymr_broad.tsv scored as-is (after the ိူ/ို compound-vowel and ႀ=θ grapheme fixes below) is 0.3057 PER over 2607 rows. Unlike Thai/Lao, Shan spells tone with explicit, unambiguous tone-mark letters rather than computing it from consonant class, so the Thai tone-PLACEMENT fold (move the mark to a fixed position, keep identity/order) barely moves the number -- 0.3040, essentially unchanged -- confirming that prior does not transfer here. Folding tone IDENTITY out entirely on both sides (this spec emits all 6 tone marks; scripts/fold_shn_notation.py) gives 0.2547, just above the 0.25 production threshold. Folding vowel length ⟨ː⟩ as well (a notation dimension the gold transcribes inconsistently in some rows) gives 0.2777. The residual above this ceiling is a real, uninvestigated segmental gap (word-boundary/compounding errors in multi-syllable entries), not a tone-notation artifact.
